arxiv-2007-11629.title: Efficient Bayesian phase estimation using mixed priors
arxiv-2007-11629.creator: Ewout van den Berg
arxiv-2007-11629.description: Abstract We describe an efficient implementation of Bayesian quantum phase estimation in the presence of noise and multiple eigenstates. The main contribution of this work is the dynamic switching between different representations of the phase distributions, namely truncated Fourier series and normal distributions.

arxiv-2102-11351.title: Generative Archimedean Copulas
arxiv-2102-11351.creator: Yuting Ng, Ali Hasan, Khalil Elkhalil, Vahid Tarokh
arxiv-2102-11351.description: Abstract We propose a new generative modeling technique for learning multidimensional cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) in the form of copulas. Specifically, we consider certain classes of copulas known as Archimedean and hierarchical Archimedean copulas, popular for their parsimonious representation and ability to model different tail dependencies.

arxiv-2104-09491.title: Multi-messenger Implications of Sub-PeV Diffuse Galactic Gamma-Ray Emission
arxiv-2104-09491.creator: Ke Fang, Kohta Murase
arxiv-2104-09491.description: Abstract The diffuse Galactic gamma-ray flux between 0.1 and 1 PeV has recently been measured by the Tibet AS γ \gamma Collaboration. The flux and spectrum are consistent with the decay of neutral pions from hadronuclear interactions between Galactic cosmic rays and the interstellar medium (ISM).

arxiv-2106-08281.title: A Horseshoe mixture model for Bayesian screening with an application to light sheet fluorescence microscopy in brain imaging
arxiv-2106-08281.creator: Francesco Denti, Ricardo Azevedo, Chelsie Lo, Damian Wheeler, Sunil P. Gandhi, Michele Guindani, Babak Shahbaba
arxiv-2106-08281.description: Abstract In this paper, we focus on identifying differentially activated brain regions using a light sheet fluorescence microscopy – a recently developed technique for whole-brain imaging. Most existing statistical methods solve this problem by partitioning the brain regions into two classes: significantly and non-significantly activated.

arxiv-2108-07673.title: 0.8% Nyquist computational ghost imaging via non-experimental deep learning
arxiv-2108-07673.creator: Haotian Song, Xiaoyu Nie, Hairong Su, Hui Chen, Yu Zhou, Xingchen Zhao, Tao Peng, Marlan O. Scully
arxiv-2108-07673.description: Abstract We present a framework for computational ghost imaging based on deep learning and customized pink noise speckle patterns. The deep neural network in this work, which can learn the sensing model and enhance image reconstruction quality, is trained merely by simulation.

arxiv-2204-01773.title: Contracts with Information Acquisition, via Scoring Rules
arxiv-2204-01773.creator: Maneesha Papireddygari, Bo Waggoner
arxiv-2204-01773.description: Abstract We consider a principal-agent problem where the agent may privately choose to acquire relevant information prior to taking a hidden action. This model generalizes two special cases: a classic moral hazard setting, and a more recently studied problem of incentivizing information acquisition (IA).

arxiv-2206-12414.title: Modeling Continuous Time Sequences with Intermittent Observations using Marked Temporal Point Processes Journal: TIST Volume: 1 1 1 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3545118 CCS: Information systems Data stream mining
arxiv-2206-12414.creator: Vinayak Gupta, Srikanta Bedathur, Sourangshu Bhattacharya, Abir De
arxiv-2206-12414.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vinayak Gupta, Srikanta Bedathur, Sourangshu Bhattacharya, Abir De. A large fraction of data generated via human activities such as online purchases, health records, spatial mobility etc. can be represented as a sequence of events over a continuous-time. Learning deep learning models over these continuous-time event sequences is a non-trivial task as it involves modeling the ever-increasing event timestamps, inter-event time gaps, event types, and the influences between different events within and across different sequences.

arxiv-2306-03408.title: Agents Explore the Environment Beyond Good Actions to Improve Their Model for Better Decisions
arxiv-2306-03408.creator: Matthias Unverzagt
arxiv-2306-03408.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Matthias Unverzagt. Improving the decision-making capabilities of agents is a key challenge on the road to artificial intelligence [ 25 ] . To improve the planning skills needed to make good decisions, MuZero’s agent [ 17 , 10 , 1 , 18 , 13 , 7 ] combines prediction by a network model and planning by a tree search using the predictions. MuZero’s learning process can fail when predictions are poor but planning requires them [ 28 ] .

arxiv-2403-04461.title: Geometric approach to i-quantum group of affine type D \mathrm{D}
arxiv-2403-04461.creator: Quanyong Chen, Zhaobing Fan
arxiv-2403-04461.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Quanyong Chen, Zhaobing Fan. In this paper, we study the structures of Schur algebra and Lusztig algebra associated to partial flag varieties of affine type D \mathrm{D} . We show that there is a subalgebra of Lusztig algebra and the quantum groups arising from this subalgebras via stabilization procedures is a coideal subalgebra of quantum group of affine 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 \mathfrak{sl} type.

arxiv-2409-01118.title: Soft-lockins in Public Sector Acquisitions of Open Source Software-solutions: A Case Study on a Municipal E-Service Platform
arxiv-2409-01118.creator: Per Persson
arxiv-2409-01118.description: Abstract Background: Open Source Software (OSS) is often seen as an option to mitigate risks of lock-ins. Yet, single-vendor OSS can still result in soft lock-ins due to knowledge asymmetries and technical barriers. Aim: This study explores actors that render such soft lock-ins.

arxiv-2501-02796.title: GraphDART: Graph Distillation for Efficient Advanced Persistent Threat Detection
arxiv-2501-02796.creator: Saba Fathi Rabooki, Bowen Li, Falih Gozi Febrinanto, Ciyuan Peng, Elham Naghizade, Fengling Han, Feng Xia
arxiv-2501-02796.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Saba Fathi Rabooki, Bowen Li, Falih Gozi Febrinanto, Ciyuan Peng, Elham Naghizade, Fengling Han, Feng Xia. Cyber-physical-social systems (CPSSs) have emerged in many applications over recent decades, requiring increased attention to security concerns. The rise of sophisticated threats like Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) makes ensuring security in CPSSs particularly challenging.

arxiv-2510-10744.title: How Patterns Dictate Learnability in Sequential Data
arxiv-2510-10744.creator: Mario Morawski, Anaïs Després, Rémi Rehm
arxiv-2510-10744.description: Abstract Sequential data—ranging from financial time series to natural language—has driven the growing adoption of autoregressive models. However, these algorithms rely on the presence of underlying patterns in the data, and their identification often depends heavily on human expertise. Misinterpreting these patterns can lead to model misspecification, resulting in increased generalization error and degraded performance.

plaw-115-186-2018.creator: United States Congress
plaw-115-186-2018.description: Public Law 115-186 (2018): National Veterans Memorial and Museum Act

pmc-10513223.title: Evaluation of the operation status of the residential land market in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region of China and its spatiotemporal pattern characteristics
pmc-10513223.creator: Xin Chen, Can Li, Huixia Li, Jingfeng Ge, Wengang Wang, Pengfei An, Jun Yang, Jun Yang, Jun Yang
pmc-10513223.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Exploring the operation status and patterns of urban land markets is an important theoretical and practical topic for promoting coordinated socio-economic development. In this study, the operation status of the residential land market in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and the characteristics of its pattern were analyzed using the composite index method and the 3σ rule of the normal distribution and taking the 174 counties in Beijing, Tianjin, and Hebei, China, as the research objects.

pmc-11448311.title: Asthma control in severe asthma and occupational exposures to inhalable asthmagens
pmc-11448311.creator: Gareth I Walters, Christopher Reilly, Nicole Le Moual, Christopher C Huntley, Hanan Hussein, Julie Marsh, Ali Bahron, Mamidipudi Thirumala Krishna, Adel H Mansur
pmc-11448311.description: IntroductionWork-related asthma accounts for ≥25% of asthma in working-age populations, though the relationship between work exposures and symptoms is frequently missed, leading to poor health and employment outcomes. We hypothesised that inhalable exposures at work are associated with poor asthma control in severe asthma (SA).

pmc-11651913.title: Laparoscopic approach in the surgical treatment of large retrorectal tumors: a short-term experience at a single tertiary center case series in Korea
pmc-11651913.creator: Jun Seong Chung, Han Deok Kwak, Jae Kyun Ju
pmc-11651913.description: Retrorectal tumors, although rare, pose diagnostic and treatment challenges due to their nonspecific symptoms and complex anatomical location. This single-center case series reports short-term outcomes of laparoscopic transabdominal resection as a surgical approach for large retrorectal tumors. Between 2017 and 2020, five patients underwent this procedure. The median patient age was 53.

pmc-11690684.title: USING BIOLOGICAL AGING TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE DIFFERENTIAL RETURNS TO EDUCATION AMONG BLACK AND WHITE OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11690684.creator: Mateo Farina
pmc-11690684.description: Numerous studies have documented “differential health returns” for education among older Black and White adults in the United States. Despite being a more select group, Black older adults with higher levels of education see a smaller return in health risk declines than White older adults. This pattern has been observed for cardiovascular and metabolic conditions, disability, and mortality.

pmc-12327075.title: High iron in mouse olfactory ensheathing cells at the glia limitans in the olfactory bulb underlies MRI T 2 * hypointensity
pmc-12327075.creator: Li Liu, Jung-Hwa Tao-Cheng, Hari Rallapalli, Stephen Dodd, Nadia Bouraoud, Alan P Koretsky
pmc-12327075.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Brain iron is important for normal function, and aberrantly high iron is often associated with neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. Oligodendrocytes are a major source of iron in brain as are iron-laden activated macrophages and microglia. T2*-weighted MRI detected a large decrease in signal at the olfactory nerve layer (ONL) in normal young mice over the period of 3 to 12 weeks of age, consistent with iron accumulation in this region. This signal change was most prominent in the inner nerve fiber layer (iNFL).

pmc-12432199.title: Study on the evolution and transport pattern of overburden fracture induced by mining in cave mines
pmc-12432199.creator: Yuan Zhang, Mengtang Xu, Dezhong Kong, Yujun Zuo, Guiyi Wu, Fi Chen, Yang Zhou
pmc-12432199.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Coal mines located in southwestern China are generally faced with the complex situation of repeated mining of coal seams in areas with dense karst caves. pmc-12606925.title: Explore the U-shape between the stress hyperglycemia ratio and diabetes or prediabetes with depressive symptoms in United States adults: insights in NHANES 2005–2018
pmc-12606925.creator: Mingzhu Wang, Chengchao Peng, Tingting Jiang, Danping Li, Chong Lu, Min Lu
pmc-12606925.description: BackgroundDiabetes is a prevalent health problem worldwide, depression is a common psychological complication in diabetics, and studies have now confirmed that diabetes with depressive symptoms is associated with blood glucose levels. Stress hyperglycemic ratio (SHR) can reflect the collective transient elevation of blood glucose during acute stress.

pmc-13325788.title: AI-based prediction of dengue incidence using climatic, environmental, and socio-demographic factors: an ensemble random forest approach with agile system development
pmc-13325788.creator: Tri Baskoro Tunggul Satoto, Nur Alvira Pascawati, Roger Frutos, Erizal, Triwibowo Ambar Garjito, Marko Ferdian Salim
pmc-13325788.description: BackgroundDengue transmission in Indonesia is shaped by interacting climatic, environmental, and socio-demographic factors, yet most forecasting systems remain static and vulnerable to data shifts. There is a critical need for adaptive, data-driven early-warning frameworks that integrate multiple predictor domains while preventing methodological biases such as information leakage.

pmc-13583108.title: Plant Metabolites Screening Identifies 7‐epi‐10‐Deacetyltaxol Inhibiting Cell Division by Interfering With the Cell Cycle and Microtubule Organization
pmc-13583108.creator: Yan‐Jie Zhang, Yu‐Xuan Bai, Geng G Tian, Bin Zhang, Ding‐Yi Lu, Qing‐Ping Yao, Wen‐Hao Tian, Xiao‐Na Wei, Jing‐Ting Yang, Ze‐Yu Xiong, Yi Lu, Yu‐Tong Jiang, Chun‐Hui Cai, Yu‐Ming Lu, Xian‐Qing Jia, Li‐Li Jing, Bao‐Jun Yang, Ying‐Xin Qi, Xin‐Xin Han, Ji Wu, Wen‐Hui Lin
pmc-13583108.description: Plants produce a considerable number of metabolites, and many of them appear to interfere with certain cellular processes such as cell division. For example, taxanes produced by Taxus are known as anti‐cancer drugs that stabilize microtubules and prevent the cell from dividing normally. Disorder of cell division also leads to abnormal growth and development in plants.
